title: How To Get Your Web Game To 60 FPS | AI Gaming Festival
author: bingewavecinema
selftext:
Look in the upper left corner; the video above shows how I've gotten part of a web game to get up to 60 FPS, which is good for a web game rendering 3D object. And it shows all the of performance metrics that are being measured.

Then it shows another section where FPS falls all a cliff to 2.4 FPS. This was actually tested and picked up AI.

In the AI Gaming Festival, we are having a session all about how to [optimize web games performance with AI.](https://www.glitch.fun/gameshows/9eadde86-a1b2-4882-86e4-a3e9e2e08814/schedule/01a0353d-a068-7154-9558-82d719cd7df4/standalone)

I think this is a critical talking point because there a few web games that spend a lot of time polishing and sometimes are virtually unplayable, and the prompt "optimize my web game" is not specific enough.

Better token utilization for vibe coders is knowing what tell the AI to measure and fix: LODs, compression, draw calls, triangles, gpu vs cpu, etc.

RSVP session while its free.

replies.author: bingewavecinema
replies.body:
1. The more complex the game, that less likely that is to work
2. The AI can completely optimize the wrong aspects of your game that you don't want optimize as AI is often lazy and aims to what is done the fast, not necessary what is correct

Example, you have an open world 3D game, and you have different graphic quality settings of low, medium, high and ultra. Everything rendered on ultra has a lot of triangles and draw calls. AI looks at the issue and just puts the default graphic settings on medium, problem solved you're at 60 FPS! But at the cost of the user experience.

More advanced, you want users to have the best graphical experience possible, but you realize that items for off into the distance are tiny, and don't need the same level of rendering. So you tell your AI:

"I want you optimize my LODs with kind of kind of rendering:  
 \- Object within 100 meters of the user render on ultra for the quality  
\- Objects between 100 and 400 meters render on high  
\- Object between greater than 400 meters render on medium  
"

You hit 60 fps with this approach and keep the user quality. A basic example of knowing that to tell the AI to tune and how that its best for your games experience.

comments.author: gloewchen
comments.body:
I vibe-coded a profiling tool in my game. This measures Frames, draw calls, and other things.  
For example:  
| Frame ms | 14.2 | 12.9 | 21.3 | 39.9 | 438.6 |

| Tick ms | 12.01 | 11.2 | 18.5 | 26 | 139.5 |

| Rendering ms | 8.84 | 7.9 | 13.9 | 18.8 | 120.7 |

| GPU ms | 2.67 | 2.56 | 4.06 | 4.85 | 10.42 |

| Drawcalls | 476.44 | 409 | 817 | 878 | 962 |

| Recorder ms | 0 | 0 | 0 | 0.1 | 0.2 |

What AI does after deep a analyse it optimizes my InstancedGroups, and it runs much better. :)

replies.author: bingewavecinema
replies.body:
Thats awesome! COngrats on that, and I am assuming that at 500+ draw calls, its a PC game.

The point of the session is that many vibe coders don't know about drawcalls, gpu ms, ticks, etc. So they can get "lost in the sauce" vs if they knew the basic concepts of optimizations, they can better tell the AI what to do and look for, and better use their tokens.

comments.author: HealthPuzzleheaded
comments.body: I let it build profiling and replay tools so we can figure out which part of the world or which feature or asset eats too much budget. then I let it research online optimization techniques for this specific issue we identified. Then we look both at the options and what would need to be done to implement it and then I usually just pick one and the AI takes care of the rest. Then we check if the performance issue was resolved.
